chunks: 163/3 - My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba narrated to us from Hamdan ibn Sulayman, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih, from Alqama, who said:

Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said — and I had said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, inform me of whose testimony is to be accepted and whose testimony is not to be accepted. So he said: O Alqama, whoever is upon the natural disposition (fitra) of Islam, his testimony is accepted. He said: So I said to him: Is the testimony of one who commits sins accepted? So he said: O Alqama, if the testimony of those who commit sins were not accepted, then only the testimonies of the prophets and the successors (blessings of Allah be upon them) would be accepted, because they are the infallible ones, unlike the rest of creation. So whoever you do not see with your own eyes committing a sin, or two witnesses have not testified against him regarding that, then he is from the people of justice and concealment, and his testimony is accepted, even if he is sinful within himself. And whoever backbites him with what is actually in him, he has exited the guardianship of Allah the Mighty and Majestic and entered the guardianship of Satan.

And indeed my father narrated to me, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them): that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever backbites a believer with what is actually in him, Allah will never unite them in Paradise; and whoever backbites a believer with what is not in him, then the bond between them has been severed, and the backbiter will dwell in the Fire forever therein — and wretched is the destination.
Alqama said: So I said to al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): O son of the Messenger of Allah, indeed the people attribute to us the grandest of matters, and our chests have been constricted by that.

So he (peace be upon him) said: O Alqama, indeed the contentment of the people cannot be possessed, and their tongues cannot be controlled. So how would you be safe from what even the prophets of Allah, His messengers, and His proofs (peace be upon them) were not safe from? Did they not accuse Yusuf (peace be upon him) of desiring adultery? Did they not accuse Ayyub (peace be upon him) of being afflicted due to his sins? Did they not accuse Dawud (peace be upon him) of following a bird until he looked at the wife of Uriah and desired her, and that he sent her husband ahead of the Ark until he was killed, then married her? Did they not accuse Musa (peace be upon him) of being impotent, and they harmed him until Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was eminent in the sight of Allah? Did they not accuse all the prophets of Allah of being sorcerers seeking worldly gain? Did they not accuse Maryam daughter of Imran (peace be upon them both) of becoming pregnant with Isa by a carpenter named Yusuf? Did they not accuse our Prophet Muhammad (may Allah bless him and his family) of being an insane poet? Did they not accuse him of desiring the wife of Zayd ibn Haritha and not ceasing until he took her for himself? Did they not accuse him on the Day of Badr of taking a red velvet garment from the spoils for himself? Until Allah made him prevail over the velvet and cleared His Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) of betrayal, and revealed in His Book: 'It is not for a prophet to embezzle. Whoever embezzles will come with what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection' (3:161). Did they not accuse him (may Allah bless him and his family) of speaking from desire regarding his cousin Ali (peace be upon him)? Until Allah belied them, the Glorified said: 'He does not speak from desire. It is nothing but revelation inspired' (53:3-4). Did they not accuse him of lying in his claim that he is a messenger from Allah to them? Until Allah revealed to him: 'Indeed, messengers before you were denied, and they were patient over denial and harm until Our help came to them' (6:34). And one day he said: 'Last night I was taken up to heaven.' So it was said: 'By Allah, he did not leave his bed the whole night.' And what they said about the successors (peace be upon them) is even more than that. Did they not accuse the Master of the Successors (peace be upon him) of seeking the worldly life and kingship, that he preferred sedition over stillness, that he shed the blood of Muslims unlawfully, and that if there were any good in him, Khalid ibn al-Walid would not have been ordered to strike his neck? Did they not accuse him (peace be upon him) of wanting to marry the daughter of Abu Jahl over Fatima (peace be upon her), and that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) complained about him on the pulpit to the Muslims, saying: 'Indeed Ali wants to marry the daughter of the enemy of Allah over the daughter of the Prophet of Allah. Surely Fatima is a piece of me — whoever harms her has harmed me, whoever makes her happy has made me happy, and whoever irritates her has irritated me'? Then al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: O Alqama, how astonishing are the claims of the people about Ali (peace be upon him)! How vast is the gap between those who say 'he is a worshiped lord' and those who say 'he is a disobedient slave of the One who is worshiped'! And indeed, the statement of those who attribute disobedience to him was lighter upon him than the statement of those who attribute lordship to him. O Alqama, did they not say about Allah the Mighty and Majestic that He is the third of three? Did they not liken Him to His creation? Did they not say He is time? Did they not say He is the celestial sphere? Did they not say He is a body? Did they not say He is a form? Exalted is Allah far above that with great exaltation. O Alqama, indeed the tongues that dare to attribute to the Essence of Allah — exalted is His mention — what is unbefitting of His Essence, how could they be restrained from attributing to you what you dislike! So seek help from Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He bequeaths it to whomever He wills among His servants, and the good end is for the pious. For indeed, the Children of Israel said to Musa (peace be upon him): 'We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us' (7:129). So Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: Say to them, O Musa: 'Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the earth, so that He may see how you act' (7:129).

key_terms.المعصومون: Al-Ma'sumun — the infallible ones, referring to the prophets and their successors
key_terms.شهادة: Testimony — legal witness testimony in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.عصمة: Isma — infallibility, divine protection from sin (for prophets and Imams)
key_terms.غيبة: Ghiba — backbiting, speaking ill of someone behind their back even with truth
key_terms.فطرة: Fitra — the natural primordial disposition toward Islam
key_terms.ولاية: Wilaya — guardianship, divine protection and authority

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about testimony, backbiting, and the false accusations against prophets?
ai.summary: In this remarkable hadith from al-Amali of al-Saduq, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) responds to Alqama's questions about legal testimony and backbiting. The Imam establishes that anyone on the fitra of Islam has valid testimony unless witnessed sinning, and that backbiting — even with truth — expels one from divine protection. When Alqama complains about false accusations against the Shia, the Imam provides a powerful consolation by systematically cataloguing the false accusations leveled against every major prophet (Yusuf, Ayyub, Dawud, Musa, Maryam, and Muhammad) and Imam Ali, showing that slander is the universal fate of God's chosen ones, and even God Himself is not spared false attributions.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Muhammad b. Qutayba narrated to us from Hamdan b. Sulayman from Nuh b. Shu`ayb from Muhammad b. Isma`il from Salih from `Alqama.

He said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as): O son of the Messenger of Allah! Inform me of whose testimony is to be taken, and whose testimony is not to be accepted. So, he said: O `Alqama! Whoever is upon the nature (fitra) of Islam, his testimony is accepted.  He said: So, I said to him: The testimony of one who is guilty of sins is accepted? So, he said: O `Alqama! If the testimony of one who is guilty of sins were not accepted, then only the testimony of the prophets and the deputies (s) would be accepted, because they are immaculate, unlike the rest of the creation. So, whoever you do not see sinning with your eyes, or whoever has not been found guilty by two witnesses, is considered to be from the people of justice, shielded [of their private sins] – his testimony would be accepted even if he had hidden his sin in himself. Whoever exposes that (i.e. someone else’s private sin) will have exited the wilaya of Allah and entered the wilaya of Satan.

My father narrated to me from his father from his forefathers (as) that the Messenger of Allah (s) said: “Whoever exposes the secret of a believer, Allah will never unite them in Paradise; and whoever falsely accuses a believer, then the hedge between them will be broken, and the accuser will be in the Fire forever in the misery of fate.”
`Alqama said: So, I said to al-Sadiq (as): O son of the Messenger of Allah! The people have accused us of the grandest of matters, and this has narrowed our chests.

So, he (as) said: O `Alqama! The contentment of the people does not rule, and their tongues do not impinge on anything. How would you not submit to what even the prophets of Allah, His messengers, and His Proofs were not spared of? Did they not accuse Yusuf (as) of desiring adultery? Did they not accuse Ayyub (as) of facing tribulation due to his sins? Did they not accuse Dawud (as) of following a bird, until he looked at the wife of Uriah and desired her; and that he sent her husband before his coffin (i.e. ahead of the frontlines of battle) until he was killed, then marrying her? Did they not accuse Musa (as) of being impotent until Allah freed him from what they had said? For, in the sight of Allah, he was a paragon. Did they not accuse all the prophets of Allah of being sorcerers in the pursuit of this world? Did they not accuse Maryam bt. `Imran (as) of becoming pregnant with `Isa by way of a carpenter man named Yusuf? Did they not accuse our prophet, Muhammad (s), of being an insane poet? Did they not accuse him of desiring the wife of Zayd b. Haritha, and that he did not stop until he secured her for himself? Did they not accuse him on the Day of Badr, that he had taken a red velvet [garment] for himself from the spoils? This was until Allah had made him overcome the velvet, dissociated His Prophet (s) from betrayal, and revealed this verse regarding it, “It is not for a prophet to embezzle. Whoever embezzles will be brought with what he had embezzled on the Day of Resurrection.” [3:161] Do they not accuse him (s) of speaking out of his desires with regards to his cousin `Ali (as)? This was until Allah belied them, “He does not speak out of his desires. This is not but an inspired revelation.” (53:3-4) Do they not accuse him of lying in his saying that he is a messenger from Allah to them? This was until Allah revealed the following to him, “Surely, messengers before you were belied, but they patiently endured rejection until Our help came to them.” [6:34] One day, he had said: “Yesterday, I was made to ascend to heaven.” So, it was said: “By Allah, he did not leave his bed for the whole night.” They have said even more than this about the deputies (as). Did they not accuse the Master of the Deputies (as) of pursuing this world and rulership; that he had preferred sedition over stillness, that he unjustly shed the blood of Muslims; and that, if there were any good in him, he would not have called for the neck of Khalid b. al-Walid to be struck? Do they not accuse him (as) of wanting to marry the daughter of Abi Jahl over Fatima (sa), and that the Messenger of Allah (s) expressed his concern over him on the pulpit to the Muslims, saying: “`Ali wants to marry the daughter of the enemy of Allah over the daughter of the Prophet of Allah. Surely, Fatima is a piece of me – so, whoever harms her has harmed me, whoever makes her happy has made me happy, and whoever irritates her has irritated me”? Then, al-Sadiq (as) said: O `Alqama! How astonishing are the claims of the people against `Ali (as)! How many have said: “he is a worshiped lord”, and how many have said: “he is a disobedient slave of the One who is worshiped”?! The accusation that he was disobedient is lighter than the accusation that he is a [divine] lord. O `Alqama! Do they not say that Allah is the Third of Three? Do they not make Him and His creation alike? Do they not say: “He is time”? Do they not say: “He is space”? Do they not say: “He is a body”? Do they not say: “He is a form”? Allah is high above that. O `Alqama! The tongues ascribe to the Essence of Allah that which cannot be attributed to it – so, why do you get confined when they ascribe what you hate to you?! Seek help from Allah and be patient. The Earth belongs to Allah, He bequeaths it to whomever He wills from His servants, and the end will be for the pious. Surely, the Children of Israel said to Musa (as): “We have always been oppressed – before and after you came.” [7:129] So, Allah said: “Say to them, O Musa: ‘Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you vicegerents in the Earth, so that you may see what you will do.’” [7:129]
